newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM urges separate bank regulatory body - Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM urges separate bank regulatory body - Jiji.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Tuesday that a new regulatory body should take over the Ministry of Finance's (MOF) role of inspecting and supervising financial institutions, Jiji news agency reported.
Hashimoto, speaking in Manila after the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting, said that establishing such a regulatory body within MOF was not an option, Jiji said.

He added that it would be better for a single regulatory body to oversee all financial institutions -- banks, brokerage houses and agricultural financial firms -- which are now supervised by different ministries.
Asked whether the organisation should be completely independent from MOF, which has been criticised for its handling of bank problems, Hashimoto said: "Can such organisation cope with emergencies?

"Supervising means we have to deal with cases of sudden failures. We have to consider the possibility of losing time while discussing the matter with other ministries if it was an (completely) independent body."

Hashimoto's Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and two other parties in a loose alliance with his minority government have agreed to carry out reforms of MOF, including the hiving off of the supervisory and inspection function of the ministry to a separate body.
There have been on-going discussions as to whether such body should be a powerful, fully independent body like the Fair Trade Commission, or an organisation that would have some affiliation with MOF.
Recently, a senior LDP official said that such a body should be affiliated with the Prime Minister's Office.
